title: Portfolio Filter Volume and the Pricing of a Program: Indoor Air Quality & Filtration Programs
content:
## Basis

Filter volume is counted across the owner's portfolio before a program under the Indoor Air Quality & Filtration Programs is priced. The volume is the sum of the covered units over that owner's programs in active or pending renewal status, plus the program being priced; quoted, suspended, expired, cancelled and declined programs are not counted. A portfolio above forty covered units is priced at the stocking rate rather than the order rate, which lowers the per-unit charge of every program the owner holds at their next renewal, not immediately. Each program is otherwise priced from its own tier's annual fee and its own tier's per-unit charge for its own units.

## The annual price of one program

The annual price of a program is the tier's annual program fee, plus the tier's annual charge per covered unit multiplied by the program's covered units, the total rounded to the cent. The fee and the per-unit charge are those of the tier the program is held at, read from the program fee schedule of the tier; the units are the program's own covered units, not the portfolio volume.

*Figure worked on hypothetical inputs.* Suppose a tier whose annual program fee is 1,000 USD and whose per-unit charge is 300 USD per unit per year, and a program covering 12 units at that tier. The per-unit part is 300 multiplied by 12, which is 3,600 USD; the annual price is 1,000 plus 3,600, which is 4,600.00 USD. The figures are chosen for illustration and are not a tier's rates.

## Counting the portfolio volume

| Program of the owner | Counted toward the volume |
|---|---|
| The program being priced | Yes, its covered units are added |
| A program in active status | Yes |
| A program in pending renewal status | Yes |
| A program in quoted status | No |
| A program in suspended status | No |
| A program in expired, cancelled or declined status | No |

*Boundary on hypothetical inputs.* An owner holds one active program covering 25 units and one program in pending renewal covering 10 units, and a new program covering 5 units is being priced: the volume is 25 plus 10 plus 5, which is 40 units, and forty is not above forty, so the stocking rate is not reached. Were the new program to cover 6 units, the volume would be 41, above forty, and the stocking rate would apply. A suspended program covering 30 units held by the same owner adds nothing to either count.

## Timing of the stocking rate

Where the volume passes forty, the lower per-unit charge reaches each program the owner holds at that program's next renewal; the price in force on a program does not change on the day the volume passes forty.
